feed.title: Sentry Engineering
feed.subtitle: Notes from the people who carry the pager.

entry.title: Sampling decisions belong at the edge
entry.summary: Head-based sampling throws away the traces you needed.
entry.content:
Head-based sampling makes its decision before anything interesting has happened, which is why the trace you want is reliably the one that was discarded three services ago. Moving the decision to the edge collector costs a buffer and buys the ability to keep every trace that ended in an error.

The buffer is the entire argument. A thirty-second window at our request rate is roughly two gigabytes of resident memory per collector, and that is the number to take to a capacity review.

entry.title: Postmortem: the retention job that deleted itself
entry.summary: A retention policy matched its own scheduler table. Ninety minutes of alert history went with it.

entry.title: What we changed after the March incident
entry.content: Three changes, none of them technical. We stopped paging on symptom alerts that nobody had ever acted on, we gave the incident commander authority to declare the end of an incident without a second opinion, and we moved the retrospective to within five working days while people still remember what they were thinking.
